notes.title: The End of Gameplay
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=g_kQLrBSrt0;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3120040/The_End_of_Gameplay/][u]The End of Gameplay[/u][/url] on Steam[/h1]

hi! droqen here! i'm going to do another announcement when the game comes out, too, but i'm reaching out to as many people as possible about my new game because... well, actually, it's really quite scary, and i wanted to release it to as [i]few[/i] people as possible, but then i did that, and then i showed it to a few more people, and then a few more, and i started yelling "[url=https://bsky.app/search?q=from%3Adroqen.bsky.social+%22kill+gameplay%22]kill gameplay[/url]" on bluesky...

it got away from me, and now this half-poem half-rant half-platformer of a videogame, which i want to describe as "[i][b]like Starseed Pilgrim, but only all the parts that nobody told me they cared about[/b][/i]," is a thing that i'm releasing to the world in a few weeks.

on the full flower moon in may.

i think of starseed pilgrim as a game that is enjoyed, mostly, by indie game devs, and this new game is even more down that rabbithole. you can tell from the title, it is about gameplay, it is something. if you want to kill gameplay too or you just want to bathe in the blood of its ending or you just want to watch in horror, maybe this game of a poem will be for you.

so, yeah, go check out my steam page for [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3120040/The_End_of_Gameplay/][u]The End of Gameplay[/u][/url]. help me with the meta-game i'm playing right now, "releasing a game on steam", make my numbers go up! put me on your wishlist!

love, droqen

thanks and see you in around a moon cycle when my game comes out!!1

notes.title: 64-Bit Support
notes.notes:
That's it, that's the whole update. I have been using a mac for years and wasn't able to play my own game! If that's your life, congrats: you can play Starseed Pilgrim now.

Thanks again to David Ryskalczyk, for reaching out and telling me how to do everything step by step and then helping me troubleshoot why I still couldn't get it working :)

notes.title: hello it's time to revisit Starseed Pilgrim, after 6.5 years!
notes.notes:
Hi! I'm a nomadic indie dev once more after years of other stuff, and trying to find my path again. Right now I'm working on a port of Starseed Pilgrim to Unity, with the potential future goals:
- Putting it on other platforms
- Putting out a nicer version that will run better on future computers and support controllers and have a pause button etc
- Adding things to it if I think of anything particularly appropriate and juicy to add to it
- Possibly re-using the engine for a proper sequel, again this is [i]if I think of anything particularly appropriate and juicy and sequel-worthy to even build in the first place.[/i]

I started a Patreon a few weeks ago. If you're interested in a closer look at what i'm up to - this Starseed Pilgrim project and whatever comes after it! - please check it out: [url=https://www.patreon.com/droqen]https://www.patreon.com/droqen[/url] (you can join a discord and chat me up about game shit!)

Also, I got my mailing list back online. If you want to keep an eye on my proper releases, the signup is on my website: [url=http://www.droqen.com/]http://www.droqen.com/[/url]



Finally, thank you so much for all the kind words and generous thoughts about Starseed Pilgrim over the years! I hope to make something twice as good and at least half as popular before I die.

notes.title: i'm making a new game. it's not really like [Starseed Pilgrim], but it's good.
notes.notes:
hi! thanks everyone here for liking [Starseed Pilgrim], or maybe just considering playing it, or maybe you are coming to this forum to badmouth it, who knows

anyway, [Starseed Pilgrim] isn't important right now. i and three of my friends joined to form the Gloam Collective a year ago and we've been working on a big, four-person project. it's a thoughtful competitive videogame with online multiplayer so you can fight faraway friends.

you can also fight nearby friends. also people who are not your friends, i guess.

notes.title: Why Are You So Terrible At EVERYTHING In A Sword Game?
notes.notes:
I’ve been meaning to write about A Sword Game since laaaaaaast yeaaaaaar. Or rather, the tail-end of last year, which was like a couple weeks ago. But then the holidays happened, my hands temporarily fell off (as they do every year), and well, here we are. Anyway, ASG is a brilliant little Ludum Dare entry from Starseed Pilgrim dev Droqen. It’s about swords, as many games are, but there’s a twist: you’re laughably incompetent. Good luck keeping ahold of your sword, much less skewering the armies of darkness like so many evil sausages. Baddies, walls, grates – everything can and will send your precious implement clanging away end-over-end. ASG is occasionally frustrating, but mostly it’s just hilarious.

notes.title: Wot I Think: Starseed Pilgrim
notes.notes:
I didn’t know a great deal about Starseed Pilgrim until its Steam release a couple of days ago. I thought it was a puzzle game. I knew it had bemused John. I was vaguely aware that clever people were urging others to play it and to talk about it. For the last seventy two hours it has dominated my waking thoughts and infiltrated my dreams. It’s a challenging, perplexing game set in a strange space that is illuminated by frequent sparks of genius.

notes.title: Now Available - Starseed Pilgrim
notes.notes:
Starseed Pilgrim is Now Available on Steam


Starseed Pilgrim is a game about tending a symphonic garden, exploring space, and embracing fate. You are a gardener, tending to empty noise and empty space to fill them both with colour. You are a refugee, building your own world away from the spreading darkness.

"Advice for playing Starseed Pilgrim: As long as you still have questions, continue."
– Jonathan Blow
